https://binaytara.org/journal/article/28: conference abstracts vol. 1, issue supplement 1, 2021 · s1-1 harsh shah , randa tao , boyu hu submission received: 2021-09-18 / published: 2021-10-04 sections introduction methods results conclusions introduction diffuse large b-cell lymphoma (dlbcl) is the most common subtype of non-hodgkin lymphoma, with 25-30% of patients presenting as early or limited-stage (stage i and ii). we aimed to investigate whether the addition of rt provided a survival benefit in early-stage dlbcl patients based on primary site at presentation comparing nodal to en disease. methods the national cancer database was utilized to identify patients diagnosed with ls-dlbcl from 2004 to 2015. landmark analysis was performed to exclude patients with the last contact within 12 months of diagnosis. kaplan-meier survival analysis was used to compare overall survival (os). cox regression analysis was used to identify hazard ratios for survival. results of the 39,745 ls patients identified, 62.9% had nodal disease, and 37.1% had en disease. compared to patients with only nodal disease, patients with en involvement were more likely to receive consolidative rt (42.9% vs. 37.2%; p<0.05). en patients were most likely to receive rt with primary bone (67.7% of 1526 patients), skin/soft tissue (60.3% of 1353), breast (58.6% of 652), testes (58.4% of 950), and thyroid (56.6% of 1059) involvement (all p<0.05). with a median follow-up of 58.8 months, the addition of rt was associated with improved 5-year os for all ls patients compared to those treated with chemotherapy alone (68 vs. 62%, p<0.001). specifically, in en patients, the addition of rt significantly increased 5-year os for skin/soft tissue (60% vs. 57%, p<.001), head and neck (63% vs. 60%, p<0.02), testicular (63% vs. 45%, p<.001), and thyroid sites (73% vs. 67%, p <0.02). conclusions though there is no consensus on optimal treatment indications for rt in ls-dlbcl, this data shows improved os in nodal-only disease and within specific en disease subgroups when rt is added to front-line chemotherapy.

conference abstracts vol. 1, issue supplement 1, 2021 · s1-1 parker woolley , elizabeth chen submission received: 2021-09-22 / published: 2021-10-04 sections background methods results conclusions background cutaneous t-cell lymphoma (ctcl) can indicate a greater risk for secondary malignancies such as breast, lung, skin, and lymphoma cancers. mycosis fungoides (mf) and sézary syndrome (ss) are two subgroups of ctcl. the primary measure was to determine if those with mf or ss have an increased risk of developing secondary malignancies and if so, which cancers compared to the general population. methods seer-18 data was sorted using the computer processing language, julia, to determine the number of secondary cancers developed 5 and 10 years after the original diagnosis of mf or ss. standardized incidence ratios (sir) were calculated by comparing the secondary cancer incidence with the age-adjusted incidence rates of the general population using nih data from 2011-2015. patients diagnosed with mf in 2001 or later were included when determining the frequency of secondary cancer for the 10-year risk. patients diagnosed in 2006 or later with mf or ss were used to calculate the 5-year cancer risk. the secondary cancers that occurred from 2011-2016 were calculated. patients who developed mf or ss after being diagnosed with another form of cancer were excluded. funding was provided by the brown center for biomedical informatics as well as the national institutes of health grants [u54gm115677] and [r25mh116440]. results there are 10,156 cases of mf in the seer-18 data set, of which 1,417 (14%) patients have an associated secondary malignancy. there are 337 cases of ss, 35 (10%) of the patients have a recorded secondary malignancy. there were 7,480 (71%) patients who exclusively developed mf or ss without a secondary malignancy. the most common secondary malignancies were non-hodgkin's lymphoma (extranodal), prostate, breast, melanoma, and non-hodgkin's lymphoma (nodal). conclusions this study, along with previous literature, verifies the increased risk for secondary hematologic and solid organ malignancies after patients have been diagnosed with mf or ss.

conference abstracts vol. 1, issue supplement 1, 2021 · s1-1 sagar ghimire , samriddhi sharma submission received: 2021-09-23 / published: 2021-10-04 sections background case discussion conclusion background in nepal, breast cancer is the second most frequent malignancy among women. even though patients are evaluated and treated as per recommendations, there are substantial barriers to treating them, including their access to healthcare, financial constraints, the ongoing pandemic, and the stage they present. here, we report a case of local recurrence of breast carcinoma attributable to all of the mentioned limitations. case discussion a 38-year-old woman initially presented to the hospital with a lump over her right breast. mammography and ultrasonography revealed growth suggestive of malignant potential. the patient, after a biopsy confirmed carcinoma, underwent modified radical mastectomy followed by chemotherapy in 2018. the tumor was 6x5 cms. histopathologically, this was invasive ductal carcinoma with surrounding lymph node metastasis and lymphovascular invasion. the patient received eight cycles of chemotherapy post-surgery and was advised to undergo adjuvant radiotherapy. she could not undergo radiotherapy because of financial difficulties. she was considered to be in remission after chemotherapy and advised to be in regular follow-ups. the patient lost follow-up because of the covid-19 lockdown, and two years later, she presented to a nearby clinic with fever and cough. covid pcr came out negative. however, she was considered to have covid-19 and kept in isolation. a month later, she presented to our hospital with growth along the mastectomy scar measuring 4x5 cm and distant metastasis to lungs on ct scan. conclusion cancer treatment is always challenging in low economic countries, and the covid pandemic and availability bias amongst healthcare workers have caused a diagnostic delay amongst these patients. similar recurrence of breast cancers has been reported worldwide, the majority of them due to reluctance to seek care despite physical findings.
https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 8th international cancer congress vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 purnima rajkarnikar sthapit , md submission received: 2026-08-03 / accepted: 2026-08-25 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background retinoblastoma is the most common primary intraocular malignancy of childhood with the worldwide incidence of 10000 to 15000 cases per live births. this study describes the presentation, stage at diagnosis, treatment patterns and follow-up outcomes of children diagnosed with retinoblastoma at tilganga institute of ophthalmology, kathmandu, over a 10-year period. methods we performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive children diagnosed with retinoblastoma at tilganga hospital between 2016 and 2025. patient-level variables included age at diagnosis, sex, country/province of origin, laterality, presenting sign and follow-up status. an eye-level subset was analysed for icrb group, stage and treatment received. the primary endpoint was advanced intraocular disease at presentation, defined as icrb group d/e. secondary endpoints included enucleation and loss to follow-up. results a total of 236 patients were included. mean age at diagnosis was 30.7 months (median 24, range 0.5-160); 132/236 (55.9%) were male. disease was unilateral in 176/236 (74.6%) and bilateral in 60/236 (25.4%). bilateral cases presented younger than unilateral cases (mean 20.1 vs 34.3 months, p=0.000054). among 226 classifiable presenting signs, leukocoria/white reflex was most common (191/226, 84.5%), followed by proptosis/orbital disease (31/226, 13.7%). in the eye-level subset, 117/142 eyes (82.4%) presented with icrb group d/e disease, including 99/142 (69.7%) group e eyes. any enucleation was recorded in 65/142 eyes (45.8%), including 55/142 (38.7%) primary enucleations. group e eyes were significantly more likely to undergo enucleation than non-group e eyes (59.6% vs 14.0%, p<0.001). among patients with available outcome data, 77/173 (44.5%) were lost to follow-up. conclusion this 10-year nepal cohort demonstrates persistently late presentation of retinoblastoma, with a very high burden of advanced intraocular disease, frequent enucleation and substantial loss to follow-up. these findings support the need for earlier detection, streamlined referral pathways and stronger retention in care in low-resource settings.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/28: expert opinion vol. 1, issue 1, 2021 · p1-7 sai pranati prakash , prakash vishnu , md , david m. aboulafia , md submission received: 2021-09-07 / accepted: 2021-09-13 / published: 2021-10-01 sections take home messages conflict(s) of interest funding information ethical statements data availability statement acknowledgements author contributions references take home messages 1. health care innovations made in response to covid-19 have benefitted cancer patients. 2. covid-19 vaccines remain a critical strategy for reducing contagion and ensuring equitable care, including for people living with cancer (plwc). 3. plwc who have had an inadequate response to initial vaccination and other people who are severely immunocompromised should be free to receive boosters. those undergoing active chemotherapy or radiotherapy and those with hematologic cancers are particularly vulnerable to serious illness if they become infected with covid-19. in this commentary, we briefly highlight several of the travails that people living with cancer (plwc) are facing, how the oncology community has adapted to the changing needs during the current pandemic, and speculate as to what the pandemic's continuing consequences will mean for the practice of cancer medicine. surviving cancer is not just a physical battle but also a mental and emotional challenge for both patients and their extended families. in this process, the interaction between the physician and the patient is crucial. achieving compassionate interchanges is essential in building a therapeutic relationship. whether it's a warm smile, a comforting hug, or a conversation, these simple, humane gestures can help cheer and console those with cancer. in the current pandemic era, these in-person interactions are often replaced by technology and the use of remote meetings with the benign intent to minimize contagion. yet, interpersonal conversations through technology tend to be dispassionate, which makes the yearning for authentic human interaction stronger than ever. complicating matters further, these technologies may not be readily available to plwc and health care personnel in many parts of the world. during the first pandemic wave, patients were understandably reluctant to go to medical centers for fear of contracting covid-19. for several months, urban medical centers, which typically would be bustling with activity, were eerily quiet. the 'quiet' was deceiving, and it soon became apparent that people were suffering heart attacks, strokes, and other medical catastrophes but were avoiding medical attention. this likely led to preventable complications and obscured the true impact of deaths either directly or indirectly attributable to covid-19. in a retrospective study from england and wales, investigators identified an 8% excess of acute cardiovascular disease (cvd) deaths among adults between march and june 2020 during the covid-19 pandemic compared with the previous six years 9 . most of these deaths were not related to a known covid-19 infection, suggesting they were most likely due to delays in seeking medical care or undiagnosed covid-19 infection. this reluctance to seek medical care resulted in a significant drop in visits to hospitals and emergency rooms in the united states and several other countries around the world 8 . on december 31, 2019, a strange new pneumonia of uncertain cause was first reported to the world health organization country office in china 1 . a cluster of these cases originally appeared in wuhan, a city in the hubei province of china. these infections were caused by a new coronavirus and was given the name 'severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2,' or sars-cov2 by the international committee on taxonomy of viruses six weeks later. it was named sars-cov2 because the virus shares significant genetic similarity to the coronavirus which caused the sars outbreak in 2002 (sars-cov). subsequently, confirmed cases of the disease caused by sars-cov-2 were recognized by the acronym covid-19 (coronavirus disease of 2019). as of august 29, 2021, there have been 216 million reported cases worldwide, with 4.5 million deaths 1 . covid-19 has deeply influenced nearly every aspect of our day-to-day lives, more so among people living with certain pre-existing medical conditions 2 . people who have a chronological age of 75 years or older are at heightened risk of covid-19-associated morbidity and mortality 3 . this is also true of people of any age who have serious health problems such as heart and lung conditions, weakened immune systems, severe obesity, sickle cell anemia, and diabetes 2 . those of color and those who, because of race, politics, or economic status, have challenges accessing medical care or who live in overcrowded housing have also been among the most vulnerable to the devastating effect of sars-cov-2 4 . cancer is also one of the underlying diseases that increases the risk for severe illness from covid-19 5 . the decline in patient visits to clinics was also very evident during the first wave of the pandemic. the united states department of veterans affairs (va) is the largest health care provider in the united states. in a retrospective study of adults using va care, there were 10,490,388 fewer face-to-face visits to va outpatient facilities during the first 10 weeks of the covid-19 pandemic than in the preceding 10 weeks 10 . the 56% decrease in face-to-face visits was partly offset by a greater than 2-fold increase in the number of video and telephone visits, but overall, there was still a 30% decrease in the number of outpatient visits 10 . telehealth visits declined as the number of new covid-19 cases decreased but plateaued as the number of cases increased 10 . until now, processes that have been engineered to curtail the spread of covid-19 have been largely empiric. some of these make good sense, such as physical distancing, frequently cleaning hands, wearing masks, and implementing robust covid-19 vaccine policies for health care workers (hcws); but other measures such as wearing gloves, using plexiglass dividers in common meeting areas, or taking prophylactic hydroxychloroquine or ivermectin may not 11 , 12 , 13 . given the danger of covid-19 spreading to vulnerable groups, basic tasks such as riding in an elevator or navigating through corridors are viewed as possibly hazardous. widespread masking, sanitizers, 6-feet distance markings, and implementation of screening protocols to assess for sars-cov-2 exposure before entry to medical centers is granted are all approaches to bring attention to the significance of good hand and face hygiene and the importance of physical distancing, and these practices assist with guarding clinics against the spread of covid-19 infection. despite measures to limit the spread of sars-cov-2, the recent variant, delta, has renewed fear of contagion just as mask mandates were being relaxed and large-scale public meetings and sporting events were starting back up 14 . in many countries, the delta variant is the dominant coronavirus strain. it is more than twice as contagious as previous variants, and there is data that it causes more severe illness 14 . although vaccinated people may still transmit the virus, these new waves of infection and death have highlighted the imperative of getting vaccines to all people and not just those who live in financially well-endowed countries. covid-19 imparts fear and anxiety not only for plwc but also for the oncology teams entrusted with their care. early in the pandemic, there was a shortage of personal protective equipment for hcws, and the world health organization (who) noted this was made worse by rising demand, panic buying, hoarding, and misuse. there was also inadequate contact tracing, isolating, and quarantines. furthermore, experts such as the united states centers for disease control and prevention (cdc), long considered the world's premier health agency, made early testing mistakes that contributed to a cascade of problems that persist today 15 . the cdc failed to provide timely counts of infections and deaths, hindered by aging technology and a fractured public health reporting system. the agency struggled to calibrate its imperative to be cautious and the need to move nimbly as covid-19 spread rapidly. in communicating to the public, cdc leadership was barely visible, its stream of guidance was often slow, and its messages were sometimes confusing, sowing mistrust. and it hesitated in absorbing the lessons of other countries, including the perils of silent carriers spreading the infection or the importance of curtailing the pandemic through the practice of mask-wearing. there was a fundamental misunderstanding that sars-cov-2 was transmitted primarily through the expectoration of large droplets rather than aerosolization of smaller particles. both the cdc and the who declared that face masks were not necessary for the public unless a person was experiencing symptoms or caring for someone who was suspected of having an infection. the effects of these missteps on health care delivery have been profound. a recent new york times article highlighted the crisis of nursing staff shortages across the united states 16 . this stems from early retirements or career shifts among nurses as they have been pushed to physical and emotional exhaustion by a pandemic that has raged on for more than 18 months. this inability to safely accommodate all the sick while health care teams struggle without basic supplies like oxygen canisters, intensive care unit beds and ventilators has led many workers across the globe to look for safer and less emotionally charged jobs. this exodus of essential hcws has had a spillover effect for clinics and units that care for plwc. the net result is an expanding array of problems that leads to delays in care as well as rushed or inadequate care. it also leads to caregiver fatigue and burnout. the "coping with covid" survey assessed us hcw stress 17 . sixty-one percent of the nearly 21,000 hcws who responded to this survey reported fear of exposure or transmission, 38% reported anxiety and depression, 43% suffered work overload, and 49% had burnout 17 . stress was higher among nursing assistants, medical assistants, social workers, inpatient workers, women, and persons of color and was related to workload and mental health 17 . the cancer journey is often alienating and lonely for those who must navigate it. not having family and friends to act as advocates and provide companionship and moral support is yet another cruel irony of a pandemic that continues to impact people of all colors and races profoundly. for most patients, it is essential to have a beloved family member or a trusted friend present during clinic visits, and lacking this support only heightens their anxiety. as a new and worldwide surge of infections is occurring due to the emergence of the delta variant, the visitor restriction policies in clinics and hospitals have once again become more restrictive, and plwc is receiving care without the benefit of friends and families at their bedside at a time when they most need support 18 . even though technology does not entirely replicate the emotions and gestures of in-person interactions, there are various applications, such as facetime, skype, zoom, and whatsapp, through which we communicate with our loved ones. these online platforms are increasingly used by plwc and their families to maintain communications amongst themselves as well as the health care team. the versatile technology of telemedicine, which was previously used as a tool to deliver care to patients in areas with limited access to health care, has assisted clinical groups with checking in on patients from a safe location and is increasingly being used by various medical disciplines during the covid-19 pandemic 19 , 20 , 21 . this has been a boon for plwc. telemedicine may occur synchronously, asynchronously, or blended with in-person care. the consultant and patient may take part virtually via fully interactive video technology in real-time or asynchronously by storing and forwarding clinical information such as laboratory results, radiology reports, and video recordings to be interpreted later. telemedicine has generally been demonstrated to be at least equivalent to in-person care, improve access, and decrease costs with high levels of patient and health professional satisfaction 22 . telemedicine may also have potential applicability for remote chemotherapy supervision, symptom management, survivorship care, palliative care, and approaches to increase access to cancer clinical trials 21 . however, telemedicine can still be limited in its usability where access to broadband is lacking; people do not have up to date computers and phones with video capabilities, and where the infirm and the elderly do not know how to use newer forms of communication that so many of us take for granted. improving communications through technology as our elderly and non-tech savvy patients struggle to utilize these new technologies, and those with lesser financial means have trouble procuring a stable web connection remains a priority. telemedicine may not be able to entirely replace in-person visits for plwc as they need to receive chemotherapy in the clinic or hospitals and often have acute care needs. side effects of chemotherapy such as neutropenic fever, intractable nausea and vomiting, and dehydration make immediate care obligatory. treating specific medical conditions promptly, such as myocardial infarction, thromboembolic complications, and electrolyte abnormalities, is also critical as these conditions influence long-term health results and survival. as testing supplies become more easily available, screening all patients with cancer for covid-19 would aid physicians with re-booking chemotherapy whenever necessary. however, we recognize the lower sensitivities of current tests and acknowledge that most regions do not have the resources to make this possible. furthermore, the initiation of numerous new clinical trials for experimental cancer therapies has been postponed during the covid-19 pandemic 23 . cancer treatment in its varied forms is the foundation of progress, and experimental treatments accessible through participation in clinical trials are frequently the last source of hope in cancer care as well as a path toward better care. consequently, creating procedures to proceed with clinical trials in oncology securely and having treatments accessible to patients for their use is fundamental in cancer care. the covid-19 vaccines (e.g., pfizer-biontech, moderna, and johnson & johnson's janssen authorized in the united states and those available elsewhere, including from russia, china, and india) continue to be highly effective in reducing the risk of severe disease, hospitalization, and death, even against the widely circulating delta variant. however, covid-19 constantly evolves, and people who are moderate to severely immunocompromised may not be well protected after they have received their initial covid-19 vaccines 24 . this is particularly true for those who receive b-cell depleting therapies and who have hematologic malignancies 24 . for these individuals, receiving another dose of the vaccine can sometimes improve protection against the disease. the cdc recommends moderately to severely immunocompromised people consider receiving an additional (third) dose of an mrna covid-19 vaccine (pfizer-biontech or moderna) at least 28 days after the completion of the initial 2-dose mrna covid-19 vaccine series 25 . however, the who has called for a moratorium on covid-19 boosters until the end of september 2021 to ensure that at least 10% of people in all countries are vaccinated before extra doses are handed out 26 . this moratorium should not apply to those plwc who have had an inadequate response to initial vaccination and other people who are severely immunocompromised. cohesive leadership at the local, state, and national levels is vital for assuring plwc receives safe medical care, as well as correctly informing the public of the risks of covid-19 so that any strategy to prevent infection is evidence-based. enforcing more efficient tactics for timely covid-19 screenings and giving medical staff access to effective personal protective equipment can increase security while providing safer interactions for both hcws and plwc. providing everyone full access to covid-19 vaccines must remain an overarching goal to staunch infection and death from this ever-mutating virus. the novel coronavirus of 2019 has given stakeholders an opportunity to rethink and foster groundbreaking ideas for access to cancer care. as we continue to adjust to life in the era of the covid-19 pandemic and with some permanent changes to daily practice patterns, sharing knowledge with responsibility and unanimity will assist in our advancements in cancer care, whether in this pandemic or in the years to come. conflict(s) of interest the authors declare no conflicts of interest. funding information no specific funding was received for this work. ethical statements this article involved no primary data collection from human participants. data availability statement this article does not contain original data. https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 8th international cancer congress vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 sajjad ahmed khan , mbbs submission received: 2026-08-16 / accepted: 2026-08-27 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background coeliac disease (cd) has been associated with malignancy, although the magnitude of risk varies by cancer type. this systematic review and meta-analysis quantified site-specific cancer risk in adults with cd compared with the general population or non-cd controls. methods following prisma 2020 guidelines, pubmed, embase, and scopus were searched in april 2025. eligible cohort and case-control studies reported ors, rrs, hrs, or sirs with 95% confidence intervals for cancer outcomes. we independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using robins-e. effect estimates were harmonised to odds ratios using a rare-disease approximation, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed using restricted maximum likelihood with hartung-knapp adjustment. results of 14,694 records identified, 31 studies met the inclusion criteria, contributing 96 study-outcome estimates across nine cancer subgroups. the strongest associations were observed for small bowel cancer (pooled or 20.52, 95% ci 5.33–78.99) and lymphoma/lymphoproliferative malignancies (pooled or 7.35, 95% ci 4.57–11.81). increased risks were also found for oesophagogastric cancer (pooled or 2.01, 95% ci 1.41–2.88) and hepatopancreatobiliary cancers (pooled or 1.59, 95% ci 1.21–2.08). breast cancer risk was reduced (pooled or 0.77, 95% ci 0.63–0.94). no significant associations were observed for colorectal, prostate, lung/respiratory, or thyroid cancers. most analyses demonstrated moderate-to-substantial heterogeneity. conclusion adults with cd have markedly increased risks of lymphoma and small bowel cancer, with more modest increases in oesophagogastric and hepatopancreatobiliary cancers, whereas breast cancer risk is reduced. cancer risk in cd is therefore site-specific rather than uniform across malignancies.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 8th international cancer congress vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 mst. suraiya nupur , mbbs submission received: 2026-07-23 / accepted: 2026-08-09 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background breast cancer is the most common cancer among women worldwide and is a major public health concern in bangladesh as well as other countries, where a lot of patients are diagnosed at advanced stages due to lack of awareness, delayed healthcare-seeking behavior, and limited access to screening facilities. although a number of wearable breast-monitoring technologies have been developed in recent years, most of them rely on smartphones, internet connectivity, high-cost hardware, or specialized wearable garments, limiting their accessibility and acceptability. this project proposes the development of a low-cost, smartphone-independent wearable breast-health monitoring device designed to support early detection of suspicious physiological abnormalities of the breasts. the proposed device will be worn as a pendant-like accessory around the neck, positioning a compact circular sensing module in the intermammary region between the breasts. the device is designed to continuously monitor some selected physiological parameters, such as localized temperature fluctuations, tissue-related electrical changes, and vascular-related physiological alterations. when persistent abnormal physiological patterns are detected, the device will provide a simple vibration or audio alert, encouraging users to seek professional medical evaluation. methods the proposed device will be worn as a pendant like accessory around the neck, positioning a compact circular sensing modulant in the intermammary region between two breasts. the device is designed to continuously monitor some selected parameters such as localized temperature fluctuations, tissue related electrical changes, and vascularity related physiological alterations. when persistent abnormal physiological patterns are detected, the device will provide a simple vibration or audio alert, encouraging users to seek professional medical evaluation. the device will be developed using affordable but sophisticated commercially available sensors integrated with a low-power microcontroller and rechargeable battery system. results the proposed device is not intended to diagnose breast cancer or replace already established diagnostic methods and tools like mammography, ultrasonography, magnetic resonance imaging (mri), or physician examination. rather it is designed as an early warning support tool that may improve breast health awareness, encourage timely medical consultation, and help to improve earlier detection pathways. if proven feasible, this device may bring a more culturally acceptable approach to promoting breast health monitoring among women in bangladesh as well as other low resource settings. conclusion unlike the cusbr-patch of mit, the proposed device will be able to collect data from larger area of the breasts as the users can easily change the position of the sensor containing modulant by hand. ai will process the data and persistent changes will be evaluated.

conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 varun nandakumar , mbbs , philippe e. spiess , md , roger li , md , petros grivas , md , sumanta kumar pal , md , ashish m. kamat , md , shilpa gupta , md , andrea necchi , md , liang cheng , md , douglas i. lin , md, phd , ole gjoerup , phd , jerry w. mitchell , md , ryon p. graf , phd , joseph m jacob , md , alina basnet , mbbs, md , gennady bratslavsky , md , jeffrey s. ross , md , neeraj agarwal , md submission received: 2026-07-11 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background the tp53 y220c base substitution mutation has become a significant therapeutic target with the development of reactivator drugs that restore tp53 function with a regulatory function in the cell cycle. however, its real-world prevalence and associated genomic landscape is not established in capc. data on concurrent genomic alterations (ga) may guide the development of combinatorial therapeutic strategies. methods 26,156 cases of capc underwent hybrid capture-based comprehensive genomic profiling (cgp) to study all classes of ga including base substitutions, short insertions, deletions, copy number changes, rearrangements and fusions. microsatellite instability (msi) status and tumor mutation burden (tmb) were determined from the sequencing data; comparisons utilized the fisher exact method. results 144 capc (0.6%) of capc cases featured tp53 y220c mutation (tp53 y220c+). patients with tp53 y220c+ capc had slightly higher mean age (70.0 vs 68.2; p = 0.020). ga potentially associated with capc primary hormonal-based therapy response more frequently found in tp53 y220c+ cases included spop (10.5% vs 1.4%; p < 0.0001). ga linked to parp inhibitor response slightly more frequent in tp53 y220c+ cases included brca2 ga (8.7% vs 3.5%; p = 0.0003) and atm ga (5.9% vs 4.2%; ns). ga in rad21 were slightly higher in tp53 y220c- capc (14.8% vs 8.3%; p = 0.029). additional selected ga, msi status, and tmb are presented in the table below. conclusion tp53 y220c is a rare finding in capc, but it may offer a potential therapeutic avenue for these patients whose tumors feature such a mutation. in addition, tp53 y220c+ cases appear to be genomically relatively distinct from tp53 y220c- capc cases and may feature genomic signatures that could influence treatment selection and trial design. study limitations include a retrospective, descriptive design, a lack of clinical data annotation, and selection and confounding biases, so our findings are hypothesis-generating.

conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 saurabh verma , phd submission received: 2026-07-15 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background androgen receptor (ar) signaling drives castration-resistant prostate cancer (crpc), but resistance inevitably emerges via ar splice variants, mutations, or amplification. characterizing the immediate, compensatory bypass pathways activated upon ar inhibition is essential to developing next-generation pathway-directed strategies and designing effective combination regimens. to isolate these rapid survival networks without the confounding genomic adaptations of chronic selective pressure, we established chemically inducible dtag (degron tag)-based ar degradation platforms in two distinct models of aggressive crpc: 22rv1 and c4-2b. methods we stably expressed an ha-tagged ar-dtag fusion construct to enable rapid, chemically induced, and reversible ar degradation. a dual-guide, single-vector crispr/cas9 approach was used to generate ar-knockout (arko) clones in 22rv1 and c4-2b lines, confirmed by targeted amplicon sequencing. temporal and dose-dependent ar loss was validated via immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, and canonical downstream target gene expression. to capture acute versus long-term compensatory transcriptomic remodeling, we performed rna-seq profiling at 3, 6, and 15 days post-dtag treatment. results ligand-induced dtag treatment mediated rapid, near-complete ar degradation in both cell lines, outperforming clinical ar degraders. ar loss induced g1 cell-cycle arrest and significantly reduced cell viability and proliferation. rna-seq revealed highly dynamic transcriptional rewiring. comparing these lineages differentiated acute, transient transcriptional stress responses from sustained bypass pathways driving long-term survival in 22rv1 and c4-2b genetic backgrounds. conclusion we established and validated a tunable, dual-lineage dtag-ar-ko platform that models distinct clinical archetypes of crpc. by capturing both the acute cellular response and subsequent chronic adaptations to ar depletion, this platform recapitulates clinical resistance trajectories while circumventing the confounding mutations of long-term selective pressure. ultimately, this work provides a robust preclinical framework to screen next-generation degraders, map co-occurring escape pathways, and can guide patient-specific combination therapies.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 yiwei wang , phd , hui li , phd submission received: 2026-07-14 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background worldwide, glioblastoma (gbm) is characterized by limited immune infiltration and an immunosuppressive microenvironment, which makes it particularly difficult to treat with immunotherapy, including immune checkpoint blockade (icb). increasing immune infiltration could be an effective strategy to enhance immunotherapy in gbm. our group has identified the actin-binding protein advillin (avil) as being overexpressed, oncogenic, and necessary for tumorigenesis in gbm. we have since developed first-in-class compounds targeting avil (science translational medicine, 2026). here, we present a combination therapy that integrates avil inhibition with anti-pd-1 blockade to enhance antitumor immunotherapy via inducing immunogenic cell death (icd). methods gbm cells were treated with a first-in-class avil inhibitor to evaluate the induction of icd. classical icd-associated markers were assessed in vitro. additionally, a vaccinated-rechallenge assay was performed in immunocompetent mice. briefly, mice were inoculated with avil inhibitor-treated gbm cells, followed by rechallenge with live tumor cells to evaluate resistance to subsequent tumor formation. furthermore, the avil inhibitor was combined with anti-pd1 therapy in an immunocompetent orthotopic gbm mouse model. tumor progression and overall survival were monitored to evaluate treatment response. tumor tissues and immune organs were harvested for immune profiling. results avil inhibitor treatment induced multiple icd features in gbm cells. in the vaccination model, avil inhibitor-treated gbm cells elicited protective antitumor immunity and reduced subsequent tumor formation following rechallenge with live gbm cells. in the orthotopic gbm model, combination therapy with the avil inhibitor and anti-pd-1 improved antitumor efficacy, as reflected by reduced tumor burden and prolonged survival. immune profiling revealed increased immune infiltration within the tumor microenvironment, together with enhanced antigen-presenting activity in the tumor-draining lymph nodes. conclusion together, these findings identify avil as a promising therapeutic target in gbm and demonstrate that its first-in-class inhibitor can be effectively combined with anti-pd-1 antibody to enhance immunotherapy.

conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 turgut dogruluk , mba, phd , matthew varga , phd , lenny hong , mba, phd , allen chen , md, mba , david tsao , phd submission received: 2026-07-15 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background her2 (erbb2) is a validated pan-tumor target, with its actionable alterations comprising two therapeutically distinct classes: amplification and activating mutations. three her2 mutation–directed therapies trastuzumab deruxtecan (t-dxd) and the oral tkis zongertinib and sevabertinib are now fda-approved, making detection of activating her2 mutations increasingly consequential. when tissue is limited, plasma ctdna enables noninvasive genotyping, but activating mutations often circulate at low variant allele fraction (vaf) and amplifications present as low-level copy gains, making analytical sensitivity the key determinant for detection. methods we retrospectively analyzed commercial northstar select (billiontoone) ctdna reports from 15,854 patients (24,105 reports) for oncogenic her2 alterations including copy number gains, missense mutations and in-frame indels. vaf and copy number were characterized per detection event, and recurrent activating mutations (>=10 patients) mapped to tumor type using diagnosis super-families. results her2 alterations were detected in 2,137 patients (13.5%) and oncogenic in 494 (3.1%), split near-evenly between amplification (n=277) and activating mutation (n=251; 34 had both). activating mutations had a median vaf of 1.03% (floor 0.01%); amplifications a median copy number of 3.52 (in plasma). the nine recurrent activating mutations showed cancer-type-specific prevalence: p.y772_a775dup, 90% lung; p.l755s (73%) and p.v777l (68%), breast-predominant; p.r678q, 44% colorectal; p.s310f spanning bladder, colorectal, biliary, and lung. activating-mutation detection was highest in bladder/urothelial (3.2%), biliary tract (2.9%), and breast (2.8%). conclusion in this real-world cohort, northstar select detected oncogenic her2 alterations at low vaf and low-level copy gain, capturing actionable her2 targets at tumor fractions below the reporting range of many assays. ctdna-derived cancer-type-specific prevalence recapitulated tissue-based patterns, validating plasma genotyping as a sensitive approach. this matters most for activating mutations in tumors not traditionally her2-screened, supporting ctdna testing to surface her2-directed therapy candidates.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 wala ben kridis , md submission received: 2026-05-12 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background traditional screening methods, such as low-dose computed tomography (ldct), have limitations, including high false positives and suboptimal sensitivity. ai, with its ability to analyze large datasets and detect subtle patterns, offers a promising solution for improving lung cancer detection rates. convolutional neural networks (cnns) and other deep learning techniques are particularly useful in image analysis, while machine learning models integrate clinical data for risk prediction. methods we systematically reviewed studies published from 2015 to 2023 on ai in lung cancer screening. eligible studies involved ai algorithms (machine learning, deep learning), specifically cnns for image analysis and support vector machines (svms) for risk stratification. meta-analysis was used to assess pooled sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values (ppv, npv), with statistical significance determined by p-values <0.05. results the pooled sensitivity of ai-based tools was 90% (95% ci: 86%-94%), with specificity at 85% (95% ci: 80%-90%). in comparison, ldct showed sensitivity of 75% and specificity of 80%. the positive predictive value (ppv) for ai tools was 78%, significantly higher than the 68% for ldct. cnn-based methods demonstrated sensitivity of 92% (95% ci: 88%-96%) and specificity of 87% (95% ci: 83%-91%), higher than other ai techniques. the p-value for cnn-based methods compared to ldct was <0.01, indicating statistical significance in enhancing early-stage lung cancer detection. ai methods also demonstrated a higher negative predictive value (npv) at 95%. the overall p-value for all comparisons was <0.05, confirming the statistical significance of ai-based methods. conclusion ai tools, particularly cnns, significantly improve the accuracy of lung cancer screening, with cnns showing higher sensitivity and specificity compared to traditional methods. these findings suggest that ai has the potential to enhance clinical practice and reduce lung cancer mortality.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 8th international cancer congress vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 shristi gupta , mbbs , kshitiz parajuli , mbbs , aron neupane , mbbs , abhisek jha , mbbs , asmita rayamajhi , mbbs, md , manash jha , mbbs submission received: 2026-08-15 / accepted: 2026-08-27 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background breast cancer with distant metastasis involving skeletal component results in complications like pain, pathologic fractures, spinal cord compression, and hypercalcemia of malignancy. mammography, ct, technetium-99m bone scintigraphy and histopathological examination assess the cancer and metastasis. anthracycline- and taxane-based chemotherapy regimens are used in both adjuvant and neoadjuvant. here, we present a rare case of early-onset, highly proliferative, invasive triple negative breast cancer (tnbc) with osseous metastasis achieving complete pathological response with palliative gemcitabine-carboplatin and zoledronate therapy. methods a 33-year-old multiparous woman presented with a painless, progressively enlarging left breast lump with ipsilateral axillary lymphadenopathy. mammographic evaluation demonstrated increased fibroglandular density. histopathological examination revealed proliferating tumor cells with intraductal extension suggesting grade 1 invasive carcinoma with negative er, pr and her2 and a high ki-67 index (40%), confirming a triple negative phenotype. cect demonstrated malignant left breast changes with lesions in the third, sixth and twelfth dorsal vertebrae; the first and fourth lumbar vertebrae; the first sacral vertebra and bilateral iliac bones with left acetabulum. skeletal metastasis was further consolidated by the 99mtc-mdp whole body bone scan. based on the triple assessment, a diagnosis of highly proliferative triple negative invasive carcinoma of the left breast with bony metastases (stage iv disease) was formulated. she received six cycles of gemcitabine-carboplatin chemotherapy with zoledronate, showing regression of breast and nodal disease and sclerosis of bone lesions. modified radical mastectomy achieved complete pathological response (ypt0n0), followed by adjuvant radiotherapy, with no evidence of recurrence on follow-up. conclusion this case illustrates a rare instance of complete pathological response to palliative gemcitabine–carboplatin chemotherapy and zoledronate in a young patient with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer underscoring potential chemosensitivity of tnbc and highlighting the role of multimodal therapy in achieving favorable outcomes, even in advanced-stage disease.

conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 kevin bera , md , zachary hanson , do submission received: 2026-06-23 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background a 72-year-old man with del(17p) stage iv chronic lymphocytic leukemia (cll), diagnosed in 1997, progressed through multiple therapies including r-chop, fludarabine, bendamustine-rituximab (br), acalabrutinib, and venetoclax. in september 2022, he developed b symptoms and elevated lactate dehydrogenase (ldh). axillary lymph node biopsy in january 2023 confirmed richter transformation to diffuse large b-cell lymphoma (dlbcl) (cd5+, cd10−). he received two cycles of r-gdp, which were discontinued because of poor tolerance, followed by two cycles of polatuzumab vedotin plus br (pola-br) as bridging therapy to chimeric antigen receptor t-cell (car-t) therapy. in may 2023, he underwent axicabtagene ciloleucel car-t, achieving a partial response, although ldh never normalized. he relapsed in february 2024 with recurrent b symptoms and pet-avid lymphadenopathy. rechallenge with pola-br resulted in a complete metabolic response. he subsequently received maintenance rituximab and lenalidomide while being evaluated for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and car-t consolidation. after eight months of remission, disease progression occurred, and brentuximab vedotin was added to his maintenance regimen. methods this case highlights the challenges of treating richter's transformation in the background of relapse/refractory cll, poor durability, and limited response to standard regimens for diffuse large b-cell lymphoma (dlbcl). richter transformation occurs in 2–10% of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (cll) patients, most commonly evolving into dlbcl. 1 , 2 per nccn guidelines, it is managed similarly to high-risk large b-cell lymphoma using anthracycline- or platinum-based chemotherapy regimens like epoch, hyper-cvad, and ofar, followed by consideration of stem cell transplant in eligible patients. however, these regimens are typically studied in younger populations and are often not viable for patients over 60. polatuzumab vedotin, an antibody-drug conjugate targeting cd79b, has shown improved progression-free and overall survival when combined with bendamustine and rituximab (pola-br) in relapsed/refractory dlbcl. 5 yet, it has not been well studied in richter's transformation. in our case, pola-br led to a strong clinical response, underscoring the potential role of antibody-drug conjugates in this setting, especially after car-t failure. brentuximab vedotin, another antibody drug conjugate has demonstrated efficacy with acceptable safety for relapsed or refractory dlbcl. in the echelon-3 trial bv + len + r demonstrated a statistically significant survival benefit compared with len + r + placebo in patients with r/r dlbcl. 8 there are several ongoing phase ii trials that are currently evaluating the safety and efficacy of adc's in richter's transformation. 9 conclusion this case of relapsed dlbcl transformed from cll illustrates the need for multiple lines of therapy and further trials, especially with car-t, in this high-risk population.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 8th international cancer congress vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-1 abhishek thapaliya , md submission received: 2026-08-03 / accepted: 2026-08-25 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background primary osseous involvement in hodgkin lymphoma (hl) is extremely uncommon and often radiologically mimics spinal tuberculosis or metastatic malignancy, leading to diagnostic delay. methods a 38-year-old male presented with severe chronic lumbar back pain without constitutional symptoms. imaging revealed multiple lytic and mixed lytic–sclerotic vertebral and pelvic lesions initially interpreted as metastatic disease. despite extensive evaluation—including tumor markers, endoscopy, bone marrow studies, and repeated biopsies—findings remained inconclusive. the patient was empirically treated for tuberculosis following granulomatous pathology and positive quantiferon, but symptoms persisted. repeat immunohistochemistry on the prior biopsy finally demonstrated cd30+, mum1+, and weak pax5 expression consistent with hodgkin lymphoma. the patient was initiated on abvd chemotherapy, achieving complete metabolic resolution and is currently under followup and remains in remission. conclusion this case underscores the importance of considering hodgkin lymphoma in chronic back pain with atypical skeletal lesions and highlights the diagnostic value of immunohistochemistry and pet-ct, especially in settings where tuberculosis is prevalent.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 wala ben kridis , md , amal bouaziz , md , ramzi tlili , md , chaima naifar , md , afef khanfir , md submission received: 2026-05-12 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background body mass index (bmi) has been widely investigated as a potential factor influencing cancer characteristics and clinical presentation. this study aimed to evaluate the association between tumor localization, bmi, and presenting complaints in cancer patients. methods a retrospective study was conducted including 151 patients with histologically confirmed cancers treated at the department of medical oncology of habib bourguiba hospital in sfax. collected variables included age, weight, height, bmi, tumor localization, and presenting complaints. bmi was categorized as underweight (<18.5), normal (18.5–24.9), overweight (25–29.9), and obese (≥30). quantitative variables were expressed as mean ± standard deviation, and qualitative variables as percentages. associations between categorical variables were assessed using the chi-square test, with a significance threshold set at p < 0.05. results the mean age was 57.1 ± 12.5 years (range: 19–82). the mean weight was 63.7 ± 13.8 kg, and the mean height was 1.63 ± 0.09 m. bmi distribution was: normal weight (45.0%), overweight (25.2%), obese (14.6%), and underweight (15.2%). the most frequent tumor localizations were gynecological (41.7%) and digestive (31.8%). obesity was present in ent cancers in 36.4% and underweight prevalence was predominant in pulmonary cancers (42.9%). no statistically significant association was found between bmi and tumor localization (p = 0.62). analysis of presenting complaints revealed a heterogeneous distribution according to tumor site. asthenia was the most frequent symptom in gynecological cancers (19%), whereas abdominal pain predominated in digestive cancers. 6% of patients were asymptomatic at diagnosis. conclusion symptom patterns appeared to be primarily driven by tumor site rather than anthropometric factors, underscoring the predominant role of disease-specific characteristics. these findings are consistent with several reports in the literature suggesting that, although bmi may influence cancer risk, its impact on tumor presentation and localization remains limited.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 reilly o cooper , phd , manan chopra , m.s. , david m. huland , phd , wen zhou , phd , allen m. chen , md submission received: 2026-07-23 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background treatment selection for advanced cancers has traditionally relied on a tumor's tissue of origin (too), but 3-5% of cancers present as cancer of unknown primary (cup) where standard workup fails to identify a definitive tumor source. too determination by pathology assessment can also be limited by tissue availability. we investigated whether methylation status and variant profiling from circulating cell-free dna (cfdna) could predict tumor too from liquid biopsy alone. methods a retrospective analysis of 6,025 advanced cancer patient samples previously submitted to billiontoone's clinical laboratory was conducted. methylation profiling of >2,000 regions with single molecule precision and ultrasensitive comprehensive genomic profiling were performed using the northstar response and northstar select commercial assays, respectively. a supervised classifier was trained on liquid methylation features from 4,447 patients and tested on a validation cohort of 1,578 patients. a sex-conditional bayesian prior and orthogonal signal from tissue-specific somatic variants detected by northstar select were then applied. class-specific rule-out thresholds were calibrated to a ≥97.5% sensitivity exclusion threshold. results in the validation cohort, cfdna methylation successfully classified the correct too as the single most likely choice in 86% of cases and among the top three diagnostic predictions in 91% of cases. the model provided tissue-specific rule-out information, excluding 10 of 12 tissue types at a ≥97.5% sensitivity threshold. tissue-specific somatic variants from the same blood draw were used to resolve a subset of difficult cases. conclusion cfdna methylation and variant profiling enabled accurate, noninvasive too prediction through a supervised classifier, supporting liquid biopsy as a decision aid in cup and other scenarios where too is ambiguous. prospective studies expanding to additional tumor types are planned to confirm the practical utility of this novel approach.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 krishna sai kiran sakalabaktula , mbbs , mukesh ram kumar kommu , mbbs , gayatri prabhakara sameer kumar majety , mbbs , abhinay theli , md submission received: 2026-07-16 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background esophageal cancer remains one of the deadliest malignancies worldwide despite advances in neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, minimally invasive surgery, and immunotherapy. we performed a transatlantic analysis to evaluate temporal changes in mortality-to-incidence ratios (mir), a surrogate of case fatality, and prevalence-to-incidence ratios (p/i), reflecting disease chronicity, to compare outcomes across healthcare systems. methods global burden of disease (gbd) 2023 data (1990–2023) were analyzed for the united states, western, central, and eastern europe. data were stratified by sex and age (15–49, 50–69, ≥70 years), yielding 24 demographic strata. joinpoint regression estimated average annual percent changes (aapcs) in incidence. linear regression with delta method uncertainty propagation evaluated mir and p/i trends, while bayesian forecasting projected incidence through 2050 (α=0.05). results incidence aapcs ranged from −3.14%/year (eastern europe females ≥70) to +1.12%/year (eastern europe females 15–49), with declines including western europe males 15–49 (−1.39%/year). all 24 strata demonstrated declining mir and increasing p/i ratios; 22/24 mir and all 24 p/i trends were statistically significant (p<0.05 and p<0.001, respectively). western europe showed the greatest improvement, with mir declines of 22.31% (females 15–49), 20.35% (males 15–49), 14.91% (females 50–69), 11.95% (males 50–69), 10.37% (females ≥70), and 9.03% (males ≥70). corresponding p/i increases reached 32.74%, 30.80%, 29.82%, 28.88%, and 26.39%. mean mir decline was greatest in western europe (14.82%), followed by the united states (5.93%), eastern europe (4.58%), and central europe (3.70%), while western europe also had the highest mean p/i increase (28.73%). younger patients and females experienced the greatest gains. divergence accelerated after 2012. bayesian forecasts project 2050 incidence of 1.03/100,000 (western europe males 15–49), 0.30/100,000 (western europe females 15–49), and 1.36/100,000 (us males 15–49). conclusion this 34-year analysis demonstrates a widespread, statistically significant improvement in survival trends for esophageal cancer, characterized by a 100% success rate in improving mir and p/i ratios across all 24 demographic strata. western europe's healthcare systems have seen population-level gains in mir and p/i ratios that substantially outpace those observed in the united states and central/eastern europe. as bayesian forecasts suggest, these findings serve as both a benchmark for european clinical excellence and highlight a widening survival gap through 2050 and suggest a need for the u.s. and eastern europe to evaluate the potential benefits of the centralized, multimodal care models utilized in western europe.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 jasmin hundal , md, mph , joel saltzman , md submission received: 2026-07-15 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background early-phase oncology trials rely on clinician-reported adverse events and performance status assessments to evaluate treatment tolerability. however, these measures are episodic, subject to interobserver variability, and may underestimate patients' symptom burden. continuous digital monitoring using wearable sensors and electronic patient-reported outcomes (epros) offers an opportunity to generate objective, longitudinal digital biomarkers that may improve toxicity assessment and support precision oncology. methods we designed a prospective, single-arm pilot study evaluating the feasibility of integrating smartwatch-derived actigraphy and weekly epros into phase i oncology clinical trials at the cleveland clinic novel therapeutics clinic. thirty adults enrolled in early-phase trials will wear a smartwatch for four weeks while completing weekly pro-ctcae questionnaires through a custom mobile application. the primary endpoint is feasibility, defined as median smartwatch wear time of ≥12 hours/day and completion of ≥80% of scheduled epro assessments. secondary endpoints include agreement between clinician- and patient-reported toxicities, time to first grade ≥1 adverse event, and user experience. exploratory analyses will evaluate longitudinal changes in activity, sleep, gait, heart rate, and heart rate variability as potential digital biomarkers associated with treatment toxicity, dose modification, disease progression, and trial discontinuation using repeated-measures statistics and machine learning approaches. results enrollment is ongoing. we anticipate demonstrating the feasibility of integrating continuous wearable monitoring and epro collection into early-phase oncology trials while characterizing the concordance between clinician- and patient-reported toxicities and identifying preliminary digital phenotypes associated with treatment-related functional decline. conclusion this study establishes a scalable platform for continuous digital phenotyping in early-phase oncology trials. integration of wearable-derived physiologic data with patient-reported outcomes may enable development of ai-driven digital biomarkers for earlier detection of toxicity, improved characterization of treatment tolerability, and more individualized monitoring in precision oncology.

conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 camron farjami , undergraduate , derek tai , ba , mojtaba akhtari , md submission received: 2026-07-15 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background inotuzumab ozogamicin (ino) is a cd22-directed antibody-drug conjugate whose calicheamicin payload causes target-independent hepatic sinusoidal endothelial injury. beyond the well-recognized risk of sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (sos/vod), a recently proposed phenotype characterized by hepatic sinusoidal congestion (hsc) without fulfilling diagnostic criteria for sos/vod has been referred to as calicheamicin syndrome. reported features include the use of ino, elevated liver function tests, abnormal liver imaging, and thrombocytopenia. altered mental status (ams) and hyperammonemia have not previously been reported as manifestations of ino toxicity and calicheamicin syndrome. methods a 28-year-old woman with relapsed cd22-positive b-all received 6 cycles of ino between february and september 2022. ino was discontinued due to hepatotoxicity and ams. a core liver biopsy demonstrated hsc without evidence of sos/vod. persistent hyperammonemia was observed throughout 2023, with a peak serum ammonia level of 123 μmol/l, notably occurring several months after ino discontinuation. the hyperammonemia was managed with lactulose and resolved as hepatic function improved. during this period, she developed ams, progressing to not able to feed herself, requiring gastrostomy tube (g-tube) placement. brain imaging showed no acute abnormalities. following discontinuation of ino and supportive management, the patient's ams resolved, the g-tube was removed, hepatic function normalized, and her performance status returned to baseline over approximately 12 months. conclusion we report prolonged hyperammonemia and ams occurring in association with ino-related hepatotoxicity consistent with the proposed calicheamicin syndrome. to our knowledge, persistent hyperammonemia and significant ams have not previously been described as part of this phenotype. although causality cannot be established from this single case, these findings suggest that impaired hepatic ammonia clearance may contribute to neurologic manifestations of ino-associated hepatotoxicity. measurement of serum ammonia should be considered in patients receiving ino who develop otherwise unexplained ams, particularly in the setting of hepatic dysfunction or sinusoidal injury.

conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 charisma desai , md , char degeorge , ba , brandon simon , rt submission received: 2026-07-15 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background cancerous lesions often demonstrate increased metabolic activity due to increased vascularity and abnormal cell growth. fdg (fluorodeoxyglucose) pet/ct is an imaging technique which utilizes this physiology to allow physicians to diagnose and monitor metastatic cancer using a glucose analog tagged with a radiopharmaceutical to highlight areas of increased glucose metabolism. while fdg pet/ct is sensitive for metabolically active cancer, other factors may lead to increased metabolic activity. among these factors are different medications, particularly diabetes medications. for example, insulin is well-known to cause increased muscle uptake which can lead to the obscuration of tumors or simply altered biodistribution which decreases relative uptake in tumors. for this reason, imaging centers provide instructions to patients to pause insulin use before an fdg pet/ct. this study aims to gain deeper insight into the effects of a newer class of diabetes and weight loss drugs, glp-1 receptor agonists. the use of these medications has increased exponentially, and their effect on the cancer patient population and metabolic cancer imaging is not well known. methods patients at an academic cancer hospital were interviewed at the time of their fdg pet/ct for use of medications including glp-1 agonists. factors that may affect imaging appearance, biodistribution, and standardized uptake value including the specific medication information, time of last dose, amount of time fasting, blood glucose level, and additional medications were compiled. images were then analyzed for signs of abnormal biodistribution and other potentially related abnormal findings. results this is an ongoing project. preliminary results show that the majority of patients taking glp-1 agonists have normal biodistribution. however, markedly abnormal biodistribution is seen in a few patients, with a few potential relevant factors including time of last dose and degree of gastric distension. in addition, patients with abnormal activity at one site have a higher likelihood of abnormal activity at another site. conclusion preliminary findings suggest that glp-1 agonists have the potential to affect biodistribution and thus interpretation of diagnostic metabolic imaging with fdg pet/ct, but this is not present for the majority of cases. conversely, these imaging studies potentially provide a unique avenue to increase understanding of this new medication's effect on metabolism and potential side effects. as the use of these medications increases and new formulations are developed, this is an important area of continuing investigation.
https://binaytara.org/cancernews/contrib: resources for cancer patients contributors ethics and disclosure policy editorial standards & corrections policy cleveland clinic lerner college of medicine dr. akriti jain is an assistant professor of medicine at cleveland clinic lerner college of medicine and associate staff at the taussig cancer institute and the leukemia and myeloid disorders program at cleveland clinic. born and raised in india, dr. jain completed medical school there before pursuing residency and fellowship at moffitt cancer center in tampa, florida. her passion for treating myeloid disorders was sparked by a close family member's diagnosis with chronic myeloid leukemia during her residency. dr. jain specializes in treating patients with leukemia and myeloid disorders, including myeloproliferative neoplasms such as myelofibrosis, essential thrombocythemia, polycythemia vera, and chronic myeloid leukemia. her research focuses on improving outcomes for patients with cml, particularly those with advanced disease. published articles ( 1 ) january 20, 2026 a leukemia specialist discusses new insights from a multicenter u.s. study on blast phase chronic myeloid leukemia, highlighting treatment patterns, outcomes, and the critical role of tkis and transplantation.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 jabra zarka , md , rodrigo rodrigues pessoa , md, phd , sounak gupta , mbbs, phd , eric chen , md, phd , patricia greipp , do , daniel s. childs , md , jacob j. orme , md, phd , r. jeffrey karnes , md , john c. cheville , md , elisabeth heath , md submission received: 2026-07-15 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background pten loss defines an aggressive molecular subset of prostate cancer and has gained therapeutic relevance with akt-pathway inhibition now approved for pten-deficient metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naïve (apmn) prostate cancer. however, pten loss is not binary, and the prognostic impact of the degree of loss, spatial heterogeneity, and genomic context remain poorly described. methods we are building a retrospective, multi-cohort mayo clinic translational study integrating pten-characterized prostate cancers with genomics, long-term outcomes, metastatic progression, and digital pathology. the anchor cohort is a radical prostatectomy tissue microarray of gleason grade group 2-5 cancers with pten and chd1 fish and >15-year follow-up. pathology accession numbers will be linked, within approved workflows, to biochemical recurrence, systemic progression, psa and imaging trajectories (to capture psa-discordant radiographic progression), and sampled metastatic tissue. a second cohort with paired pten ihc, fish, and sequencing will define assay concordance, and whole-slide sections will support ai-assisted quantification of percent pten loss and spatial heterogeneity. results in the anchor cohort (409 patients with fish; 262 in survival analysis; median follow-up 15.1 years), pten and chd1 loss — assessed by fish on gleason pattern 4 tissue microarray cores — were present in 24.7% and 18.3% of cases, respectively. on cox analysis, pten loss — but not chd1 loss — was associated with worse biochemical recurrence, systemic progression, and prostate cancer-specific death, supporting pten loss as a marker of aggressive biology. linkage to oncologic outcomes, psa-discordant progression, assay concordance, and ai-based quantification is ongoing. conclusion this study will establish an integrated clinical-pathologic-genomic framework that moves pten assessment beyond a binary ihc call. by linking depth and pattern of pten loss to long-term outcomes, it aims to improve risk stratification, flag patients prone to psa-discordant progression, and refine selection for pten/akt-pathway–targeted therapy.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 6th binaytara precision oncology summit: at the forefront of targeted cancer therapy vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-2 wala ben kridis , md , amal bouaziz , md , yasmin daouas , md , afef khanfir , md submission received: 2026-05-12 / accepted: 2026-07-28 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background chemotherapy-related toxicity remains a major challenge in oncology, impacting treatment delivery and outcomes. the cancer and aging research group (carg) score is a validated tool initially developed to predict severe toxicity, integrating both clinical and functional parameters. this study aimed to evaluate its predictive performance in tunisian cancer patients. methods we conducted a retrospective study including 140 patients treated with chemotherapy at the department of medical oncology in sfax. collected variables included age, sex, cancer type and stage, anthropometric data, hemoglobin level, renal function, and treatment characteristics. geriatric assessment included history of falls, hearing impairment, social activity, functional limitations, and medication management autonomy. the carg score was calculated for each patient along with the predicted risk of grade 3–5 toxicity. observed toxicities were graded according to ctcae criteria (grades 1–5). results the median age was 57 years (range: 19–80), with 64% female patients (90 women and 50 men). breast cancer was the most frequent (41%), followed by gastrointestinal cancers (29%). metastatic disease was present in 45.7% of cases. 73.6% of patients developed toxicities. digestive toxicity was the most frequent (52.1%), followed by hematologic (28.6%), cutaneous (16.4%), and neurological (15.7%), with lower rates of renal (10%), hepatic (4.3%), metabolic (4.3%), and cardiac toxicity (3.6%). patients aged ≥65 years experienced higher toxicity rates (84.1%). according to the carg score, 2.8% of patients were classified as low risk (score 0–5), 55% as intermediate risk (score 6–9), and 42% as high risk (score 10–19). a significant association was observed between carg risk groups and toxicity occurrence (p < 0.001). the predictive value of the test was 0.85. the corresponding predicted probabilities of developing grade 3–5 toxicity ranged from 25–32%, 50–54%, and 77–89% for low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups, respectively. patients with intermediate scores (6–9) showed a moderate incidence of mainly low-grade toxicity (59.5%, predominantly grade 1–2), whereas those with high scores (10–19) had an increased risk of toxicity (94.9%), predominantly digestive and of higher severity. grade ≥3 toxicity occurred in 12.6% of patients and observed rates of grade ≥3 toxicity were 0%, 1.5%, and 25.4% across low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups, respectively. conclusion the carg score showed good predictive accuracy for chemotherapy toxicity in our cohort. its integration into routine practice may improve risk stratification and guide individualized treatment decisions in adult cancer patients.

accepted: 2026-08-27 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background pancreatic cancer is a highly lethal malignancy whose absolute burden may rise because of population growth, population ageing, changes in age-specific disease rates, or combinations of these processes. we quantified the contemporary burden and decomposed the drivers of change across development levels and world regions. methods we performed an ecological analysis of global burden of disease (gbd) 2023 estimates from 1990 to 2023 across five socio-demographic index (sdi) groups and seven gbd super-regions. incidence, deaths and disability-adjusted life-years (dalys) were described using all-age counts and age-standardised rates. temporal trends were summarised using estimated annual percentage change. changes in deaths and dalys were decomposed using a symmetric shapley-style framework into population growth, population ageing and age-specific rate change. secondary analyses examined sex, successive time intervals and geographic inequalities. results derived global incident cases increased from 226,656 in 1990 to 578,236 in 2023 (+155.1%), deaths from 220,161 to 552,300 (+150.9%), and dalys from 5.43 million to 12.28 million (+126.0%). of the 332,139 additional deaths, population ageing contributed 172,294 (51.9%), population growth 149,062 (44.9%), and age-specific mortality-rate change 10,783 (3.2%). for the 6.84 million increase in dalys, growth and ageing each contributed approximately 3.46 million, while age-specific rate change offset 82,003 dalys. lower-sdi settings showed substantial contributions from population growth and rising age-specific rates, whereas ageing dominated in high-middle- and high-sdi settings. male age-standardised rates exceeded female rates in every sdi group and super-region in 2023, and relative geographic inequalities narrowed but remained substantial. conclusion the rise in global pancreatic cancer burden since 1990 has been driven predominantly by demographic change, but the balance of drivers varies substantially by development level and region. cancer-control planning should therefore distinguish demographic expansion from changes in underlying age-specific burden and tailor prevention, diagnostic capacity, treatment and palliative-care services accordingly.

https://binaytara.org/journal/article/12: conference abstracts - 8th international cancer congress vol. 6, issue supplement 2, 2026 · s1-1 sajjad ahmed khan , mbbs submission received: 2026-07-21 / accepted: 2026-08-25 / published: 2026-09-10 sections abstract abstract background the mortality burden associated with coexisting pancreatic cancer and cerebrovascular disease in the united states remains poorly characterised. we evaluated temporal, demographic, geographic, urbanisation, and forecasted mortality patterns. methods this retrospective population-based study used cdc wonder multiple cause of death data for adults aged 25 years or older from 1999 to 2024. deaths were included when both conditions were listed as underlying or contributing causes. age-adjusted mortality rates (aamrs) were analysed using joinpoint regression, and autoregressive integrated moving average models generated 10-year forecasts. results overall, 22,085 deaths were identified. annual deaths increased from 591 in 1999 to 1,630 in 2024, while the aamr increased from 0.32 to 0.56 per 100,000. rates were stable from 1999 to 2013, then increased significantly through 2024 (annual percentage change, 6.26%; 95% confidence interval, 5.11–8.25). mortality was higher among males, reaching 0.65 per 100,000 in 2024, and highest among non-hispanic black or african american individuals at 0.87 per 100,000. mortality increased significantly across all census regions, with the highest 2024 aamr in the midwest at 0.57 per 100,000. metropolitan and nonmetropolitan rates reached 0.45 per 100,000 by 2020. the overall aamr was projected to reach 0.76 per 100,000 by 2034. conclusion us mortality involving pancreatic cancer and cerebrovascular disease increased substantially after 2013, with persistent sex, racial, and geographic disparities.
